messages.subject: frequency modulation in animal sound
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I am trying to find a function that would enable me to get a measure for frequency modulations in the animal calls I am analyzing.
I would like to be able to extract some values similair to the ones used by the fm option of the function synth.

fm is a vector of length 3 including:
(1) the maximum excursion of a sinusoidal frequency modulation (in Hz),
(2) the frequency of a sinusoidal frequency modulation,
(3) the maximum excursion of a linear frequency modulation (in Hz).

Would this be possible. I have been playing around with for instance ifreq, but I am not able to figure it out.
Thanks a lot in advance for your help.

Greetings David Jansen

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] frequency modulation in animal sound
messages.body_plain:
Dear David,

I am not an expert in FM analysis but as far as I know there is unfortunately no tool to modelize the FM.

You can try to track the dominant, the fundamental, or the instantaneous frequency with the dfreq(), fund() and ifreq() functions respectively.

This will return a time series that you can try to describe and modelize with time series statistical tools.

Any other suggestion from other users would be welcome,

Jerome

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Release of seewave 1.6.5
messages.body_plain:
>From Ariovaldo A. Giaretta
Dear Sueur and friends, could someone help me with the attached scritp and sound file.
They have to do with Quality Factor determination.
Kind regards.

2012/12/13 Jerome Sueur <su...@mnhn.fr>

> Hi,
>
> A new version of seewave (1.6.5) was deposited on CRAN yesterday. Binairies should be ready soon.
>
> I added a new vignette to help students starting with signal analysis. I will try to improve and complete it in the future.
> Here is the link for download: http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/seewave/vignettes/seewave_analysis.pdf
> Feedback is very welcome.
>
> Thanks very much to Stefanie LaZerte and Jesse Ross for their input for this new release (see NEWS below)!
>
> Best regards
>
> Jerome
>
>
>
> ------------------------------------------------------
>
> NEW FEATURES
>         o a new vignette named 'seewave_analysis' for a short introduction to sound analysis. This vignette is mainly written for students starting with bioacoustics.
>         o meandB(), moredB(): a new argument 'level' to choose between intensity level (IL) and sound pressure level(SPL).
>         o meanspec(), spec(), spectro() and spectro3D(): a new argument 'norm' to control the normalisation of the results.
>         o sddB(): a new function to estimate the standard deviation of dB values.
>         o oscillo(): three new arguments: 'xlab' and 'ylab' to specify the name of the axes, 'cex' to specify pitch size if type is "p", or "b" or "o".
>         o sox(): a new function to call SoX. Sox is required to use the function but not to install the package.
>
>
> OTHER CHANGES
>         o ceps(): a bug regarding the argument 'alim' is now fixed.
>         o specprop(): frequency resolution is increased thanks to a patch by Jesse Ross (Cornell University)
>         o zc(): a new argument 'warning' to control the display of the warning message in case of interpolation.
>
>

--
